match.reason: None of the bank points teaches workforce planning, which means working out the knowledge, skills and ideas a business needs from staff and how technology shifts those needs; the closest matches cover starting resources, leadership, change, development and maintenance instead.

draft.title: Staffing needs
card: Before hiring, a business works out what it needs from its staff. It looks at the knowledge, skills and ideas that will help it meet its objectives.
Knowledge
what a person knows, such as food safety rules or how to read financial reports.
Skills
what a person can do, such as using a till, repairing a machine or serving customers well.
Ideas
new ways to solve problems or improve products, which staff may bring from their own experience. Technology can change all three needs, such as adding a need for digital skills.
draft.remember: Work out the knowledge, skills and ideas needed, and check how technology changes them.

a.q: Mia runs a bakery in Ballarat. She wants a new employee who can decorate cakes to a high standard. Which staffing need is this?
opts: A skill, because it is something a person can do
Knowledge, because it is something a person knows
An idea, because it is a new way to improve products
A change from technology, because decorating uses tools
a.why: Decorating cakes is something a person can do, so it is a skill. Knowledge is what a person knows, such as food safety rules, and the task here is a practical ability rather than a fact.
a.clue: Is it about doing something or knowing something?

b.q: Dev owns a small clothing shop in Geelong. He starts selling through an online store. How is this most likely to change his staffing needs?
opts: He may need staff with website and online order skills
He must replace all his current staff with new people
He no longer needs to work out what staff must know
He only needs staff who can bring new ideas
b.why: Technology can change what a business needs from staff, and an online store calls for digital skills such as managing orders. The other options go too far: the card says needs can change, not that every worker must be replaced or that planning stops.
b.clue: Think about what new tasks an online store creates.

a.best: A skill, because it is something a person can do

b.best: He may need staff with website and online order skills

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedge ('may'). Every distractor uses an absolute ('only', 'no longer', 'must replace all'), so a student can pick the answer by spotting the qualifier without knowing the idea.

b.q: Dev owns a small clothing shop in Geelong. He starts selling through an online store. Which statement best describes the effect on his staffing needs?
opts: It adds a need for digital skills to run the online store
It removes the need to plan staffing before he hires
It changes his products but not what he needs from staff
It swaps his need for skills into a need for new ideas
b.why: Technology can change what a business needs from staff, and an online store adds a need for digital skills such as managing orders and the website. Saying it changes nothing about staff is wrong, because technology can change all three needs. Planning still happens before hiring, and a new tool adds skills rather than turning skills into ideas.
b.clue: Think about what new tasks an online store creates.
